questions.explain: The Moon and mirrors only reflect light; they don't make it.
Transparent: almost all light passes; translucent: some; opaque: none.

questions.prompt: Which fact about light explains why shadows form?
questions.explain: Light can't bend around an opaque object, so a dark region forms behind it.

questions.prompt: In the Shadow Theatre, you move the puppet CLOSER to the lamp. What happens to the shadow?
questions.explain: The rays spread out from the lamp, so a puppet near the lamp blocks a wider cone of light.

questions.prompt: A 10 cm puppet is 20 cm from a small lamp. The screen is 100 cm from the lamp. How tall is the shadow?
The image in a pinhole camera is…
questions.explain: Rays from the top of the object pass straight through the hole and reach the bottom of the screen, so the image is inverted.

questions.prompt: Plan an investigation into how the distance between a torch and an object affects the size of its shadow.
questions.modelAnswer: Independent variable: distance from the torch to the object (e.g. 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 cm). Dependent variable: height of the shadow on the wall, measured with a ruler. Control variables: the same object and torch, the same distance from torch to wall, a dark room, the object held upright. Repeat each measurement and plot shadow height against distance.
rubric: Dependent variable: shadow size and how it is measured
questions.explain: Criterion B: a clear fair-test plan.

questions.text: We see non-luminous objects because they ___ light into our eyes. A shadow forms when an ___ object blocks light.
questions.explain: Light from a source bounces off objects into our eyes.
